scores.fix: Almost nobody plays AI songs, but bots do, for real money.
scores.note: Two sentences, 14 words and British spelling, and false as worded: most AI songs earn nothing and only uncaught fake plays take a slice (factlock correction 13, two Never-say rows).

scores.fix: Some days, half the new songs on one app are AI-made.
scores.note: A scale stat with no stake: frame 0 drops 'one app' (reads as half of all new music) and it points at song count, not plays, which is the wrong mechanism.

scores.note: Fresh, true, one real case with a built-in 'who did he even hurt?' that walks straight into the pot, but frame 0 leaves out AI, the fuss word.

scores.fix: An AI song can get paid without a single real listener.
scores.note: True and a little intriguing, but abstract: no AI, no victim, and 'a song can get paid' sounds odd.

scores.fix: Most plays on AI songs were fake, one app found.

scores.fix: Bots play AI songs for a slice of Spotify's $11 billion payout.

scores.fix: On one app, AI songs' biggest fans are bots.

scores.fix: Your favorite artist's pay comes from a pot bots dip into.

scores.fix: One app says most AI songs flooding it are for bots.

scores.fix: Bots fake the plays, but the money is real.

Two sentences of clever parallelism, and the stake (money) never shows.

scores.fix: Some of your monthly fee can end up with bots.
scores.note: Personal and true, but stacked hedges and 12 words drain the jolt.
Leads with the absurd image, then asks the question the video answers; a near-twin of L35.
The hottest question and the best comment bait, but it promises a listening test we can't play, so line 2 must turn to the plays by ~3 s or it reads as bait.

scores.fix: Part of your subscription can end up paying bot farms.
scores.note: 'Bot farm' is vivid and the hedges are honest, but 12 words is slow for 1.5 s.
A smart mid-video beat, not a hook: a scroller can't see why a bot that pays is a problem.

scores.fix: One app says most AI uploads aren't for you; they're for bots.
scores.note: 'Made' overreaches (Deezer spoke of uploads), frame 0 drops the attribution, and 'made for you' is ambiguous.

scores.fix: Bots playing AI songs can shrink your favorite artist's pay.
scores.note: The most precisely true 'favorite artist' line, but the qualifier eats the jolt and 'slice' needs the pot first.
A plain, true TIL about your fee, but a mild jolt with no AI or bots on frame 0.
A great personal jolt that promises a 'which song?' reveal the pot story can't give, so the turn reads as bait.

scores.fix: For years, his bots played his AI songs, and he got paid.
scores.note: A punchy tricolon, but frame 0 has no consequence and 'your apps' stretches the 'you'.

scores.fix: AI songs' biggest fans are bots, one app found.
scores.note: The strongest scroll-stop and most shareable line, but it states one app's data as universal, so 'one app' must be on screen.

scores.fix: Billions of bot plays on his AI songs got him 18 months.
scores.note: Strong whiplash, but without 'bots' it reads as prison for popular AI songs until line 2.

scores.fix: An AI song no human hears can still get paid.

scores.fix: Who's playing all these AI songs, if not you?

scores.fix: Hardly anyone plays AI songs, so why are there so many?

Two stats and a range on frame 0 make a mid-video beat, not a hook.

scores.fix: Most AI songs are uploaded for bots to play, one app says.

scores.fix: Bots playing AI songs are skimming your favorite artist's pay.
scores.note: Plain, direct, states the payoff and 'skimming' is honest about size, but with no AI it drops the fuss the topic was picked for.
The cleanest question to the viewer: true, a sticky pays/plays rhyme, AI up front, and the answer is the mechanism, though the jolt is curiosity, not anger.

scores.note: Personal and short, but frame 0 drops 'some' and 'can end up' mutes the jolt.

scores.fix: Who lost out when his bots played his AI songs?

scores.fix: You'll never hear the bot plays that cost artists money.

A strong mid-video quote card, but an exec saying 'zero-sum game' won't stop a scroller.

A true, uncanny story, but impersonation is a different fuss the pot can't pay off (FL 5.14).

Eerie, but cryptic at frame 0, and the pot can't pay off impersonation.
